decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 50 basis points, to 2.5%.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 2-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 3 percent.”

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 50 basis point reduction in the discount rate to 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 50 basis point reduction in the discount rate to 2-1/2 percent.”

changes.quote: The terrorist attacks have significantly heightened uncertainty in an economy that was already weak.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Business and household spending as a consequence are being further damped.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The Federal Reserve will continue to supply unusually large volumes of liquidity to the financial markets, as needed, until more normal market functioning is restored.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: As a consequence, the FOMC recognizes that the actual federal funds rate may be below its target on occasion in these unusual circumstances.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee continues to believe that, against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.
The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 2-1/2 percent.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.06% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.53% and moved -2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.8% would fall by about $4.00 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 4.9%, and employers added an average of -129k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.7% over the past year (August 2001); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -5 bp on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates).
